items.title: The damage boundary persists across phase and rotation

queries.summary: Three hundred calibrated injuries tested five damage levels, three anatomical locations, five phases, and four rotations, with 20 matched controls.

source.label: Genesis replicated damage sweep

metricDefinitions.name: Survival rate
metricDefinitions.definition: Survival rate counts trials with final mass of at least 1.0 after 300 post-damage steps and divides by 20 invariance trials per condition.
metricDefinitions.calculationSummary: Five phases and four rotations for each damage-location pair.

caveats: These are deterministic invariance trials, not statistically independent organisms or evolutionary replicates.

evidenceFlow.title: Calibration accuracy
evidenceFlow.detail: Mean absolute error between target and actual removed mass was 0.45 percentage points; the maximum was 1.94 points.

evidenceFlow.title: Control stability
evidenceFlow.detail: Undamaged controls retained 99.0% to 100.1% of pre-intervention mass.

evidenceFlow.title: Phase and rotation consistency
evidenceFlow.detail: All five phases and all four rotations produced the same condition-level survival boundary.

evidenceFlow.title: Observed boundary
evidenceFlow.detail: Only trailing wounds at 5% and 10% survived; every center and leading wound and all wounds at 15% or greater became extinct.

preview.note: Complete aggregate result at the damage-by-location grain.
